name: Flutter
summary: A free toolkit from Google for building an iPhone and Android app from one Dart codebase.

free_plan_covers.note: Flutter is free and open source under the BSD-3-Clause license, with no required hosted service to build or ship an app.

first_paid_usd_month.note: No paid plan. The SDK is free. Optional extras like paid CI minutes cost money only if you choose them.

portability.note: Flutter draws every widget itself in Dart instead of using native UI components, so switching to Native or Expo means rewriting the whole app.

language.note: The entire app, UI and logic, is written in Dart and compiled to native ARM code.

shares_react_skills.note: Screens are built with Flutter's own Dart widgets, not React, so React patterns do not carry over.

needs_mac_for_ios.note: Xcode is required to build and release the iOS app, and the official guide says you must use a device running macOS.

setup.step: Install the Flutter SDK, plus Xcode on a Mac for iOS or Android Studio for Android.
Create a new app with flutter create my_app.
Run flutter run to launch it on a simulator, emulator or connected phone with hot reload.
Build a release with flutter build ipa for iOS or flutter build appbundle for Android.

builder_notes: Never hardcode API keys as string literals or pass them with --dart-define. Both end up as readable plain text in the compiled app.
Code obfuscation only renames symbols. It does not encrypt strings or protect secrets. Call anything that needs a private key from your own backend.
